title: Mission: plan.md
subtitle: The dev agent runs a multi-phase plan as a mission: distill the macro-goal, delegate the build to the coder sub-agent (and lookups to scout), QA-gate each phase, then audit the acceptance ledger and clear — driven by the /goal loop.
note: Illustrative demo of mission mode, the /goal loop, dev + sub-agents, and the qa skill — recorded, not live.

blocks.text: /goal Implement ALL phases of plan.md and set it as the mission using the mission skill (distill the macro-goal, to-do list for EVERY phase, sentinel --preapproved). QA-gate each phase, then audit requirement-by-requirement and clear. Decide reversible forks yourself; don't stop to ask. --max 50

blocks.name: read_file
blocks.detail:
plan.md — 3 phases:
  P1 Billing API client (typed, retries)
  P2 Sync engine (diff + conflict-safe writes)
  P3 CLI wiring + docs

blocks.text: Distilling the macro-goal and enumerating **all three phases** up front — the ledger judges the whole plan, not just the phase in front of me.

blocks.name: mission-state.js --accept-add ×3
blocks.summary: Record the acceptance ledger — one criterion per phase
blocks.detail: p1-billing-client · p2-sync-engine · p3-cli-docs  (each MET only with cited evidence)

blocks.text: **Mission set** (pre-approved autonomous). Task list covers P1–P3; acceptance ledger has 3 criteria. The `/goal` loop will re-invoke this session each turn until the ledger is clean. Starting **Phase 1**.

blocks.name: invoke_sub_agent (scout)
blocks.summary: Read-only lookup: where does the HTTP layer live?
blocks.detail: scout (Sonnet, read-only): returns `src/http/` uses a shared `fetchJson` wrapper — reuse it, don't add a new client.

blocks.name: invoke_sub_agent (coder)
blocks.summary: Delegate Phase 1 implementation to the coder sub-agent
blocks.detail: coder (Sonnet) builds against the spec + scout's finding: reuses fetchJson, adds typed BillingClient with retry/backoff. Reports back what it wrote.

hunks.text: export class BillingClient { /* typed calls over the shared fetchJson */ }
// exponential backoff on 429/5xx; never logs the API key

blocks.text: Phase 1 built by `coder`. Auditing against the plan (typed ✓, retries ✓, reuses fetchJson ✓), then running QA before I move on.

blocks.name: qa skill
blocks.summary: Verify Phase 1 (code-only → its own tests, red-green)
blocks.detail:
No product UI in P1, so QA = the unit suite, not a browser render.
$ npm test  → 14/14 passing (incl. a red-green retry/backoff case).

blocks.text: **Phase 1 QA: PASS** — WORKS ✓ (14/14, red-green on the retry path), MATCHES INTENT ✓ (typed client with retries, reuses the shared wrapper). Recording it MET with evidence and moving to Phase 2.

blocks.name: mission-state.js --accept-set
blocks.detail: MET p1-billing-client  evidence='npm test 14/14; red-green retry case'

blocks.name: invoke_sub_agent (coder)
blocks.summary: Delegate Phase 2 (sync engine + a small status page)
blocks.detail: coder builds the diff/conflict-safe sync engine and a /sync status page. Applied the design skill's full state set (loading/empty/error) while building the page.

blocks.name: qa skill
blocks.summary: Full QA — real browser render (product surface changed)
blocks.detail:
.qa-active sentinel set (arms the render gate).
Rendered /sync in a headed browser at staging; checked loading, empty, error + a conflict.
Coverage receipt: COVERAGE-OK.

blocks.text: **Phase 2 QA: PASS** — WORKS ✓ (sync + conflict resolution verified), MATCHES INTENT ✓ (status page shows loading/empty/error, not just the happy path). A fetch/200 wouldn't have caught the blank-empty-state bug the render did. Ledger updated; on to Phase 3.

blocks.name: mission-state.js --set audit
blocks.detail: state: audit — re-read plan.md and verify EVERY requirement MET with cited evidence.

blocks.text: **Requirement-by-requirement audit vs plan.md:** P1 billing client MET (tests) · P2 sync engine + status page MET (render + coverage) · P3 CLI wiring + docs MET (built + `--help` verified). No gaps, no partial rollouts, no deferred scope.

All three phases built, QA green each phase, ledger **COMPLETE** — mission cleared and the `/goal` loop stops. Every reversible fork along the way was decided and logged; nothing needed a one-way-door stop.
